title: ARES Stage 1 Attack Scenarios Output
description: Schema for the attack-scenarios stage output from the offensive panel. Enforces ATK-NNN IDs, required narrative fields, severity, and detection-evasion analysis.

id.description: Unique scenario identifier matching ATK-NNN format

objective.description: Attacker goal — exfil what / RCE where / persistence in what

entry.description: Attack vector — file path, endpoint, dependency, or input source

primitives.description: Ordered list of exploit primitives used in the chain

chain.description: Ordered narrative — entry to primitive to escalation to objective

defender_visibility.description: What shows up in logs, monitoring, or alerts during this scenario

evasion.description: Techniques an attacker would use to avoid the visibility noted in defender_visibility

suggested_test.description: Handoff for risk-analysis-agent — input, action, expected pass/fail

target_rank.description: Exploit likelihood rank (1 = highest priority target)

novelty.description: How novel/unexpected the chain is (1 = well-known, 10 = highly novel)

cve_refs.description: Optional CVE references relevant to this scenario

prerequisites.description: Optional preconditions the attacker must satisfy before executing this chain

count.description: Total number of ATK-* scenarios produced

critical_count.description: Number of scenarios with severity critical

top_chain_id.description: ID of the scenario with the highest combined target_rank and severity

attack_classes_covered.description: High-level attack classes represented across all scenarios (e.g., memory-safety, supply-chain, prompt-injection, auth-bypass)

stage_summary.description: 200-word-max summary for downstream stages describing the attack surface, top chains, and coverage. Downstream stages read this rather than re-reading all scenarios.
